ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.claim: The prophet narratives share a refrain of God's peace and mercy, support for the messenger's mission, and reward for good deeds; this refrain summarizes the anecdotes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.anchor: It is this motif which, in fact, is the summary of these anecdotes as well.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.claim: Through Aaron, the prophets are listed chronologically; afterward their order follows each prophet's attributes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.anchor: Till the mention of Aaron (sws) all prophets are cited in the chronological order; after that the sequence is based on the attributes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r6.claim: Probably a shark swallowed Jonah; God saved him when he recognized his folly and glorified God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r6.anchor: probably a shark swallowed him but God saved him because he realized his folly and extolled the Almighty.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r5.claim: The tasbīḥ here is Jonah’s confession and plea for forgiveness in the words of 21:87, and it brought his deliverance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r5.anchor: it refers to chanting of the words

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r6.claim: As soon as the calamity struck, Jonah understood it as punishment and turned to God wholeheartedly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r6.anchor: as soon as this calamity struck Jonah (sws) it became evident to him that he had been punished by the Almighty and he turned to God with all his heart.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r7.claim: Jonah’s prayer is described as the best expression of confessing sin and seeking forgiveness from God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r7.anchor: These are the best of words which express confession of a sin and seeking of forgiveness from God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r5.claim: The apparent meaning is that Jonah would have remained in the whale until resurrection; Qatada says its belly would have served as his grave until Judgment Day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله للبث في بطنه إلى يوم البعث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r6.claim: The author declines to repeat the contradictory reports about how long Jonah stayed in the whale.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p124/r6.anchor: وذكر في مدة لبثه في بطن الحوت أقوالا متكاذبة، ضربنا عن ذكرها صفحا

SAMIN-DURR:37:144/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:144/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:37:144/r1.claim: The apparent construction attaches في بطنه to لبث.
SAMIN-DURR:37:144/r1.anchor: الظاهر أنه متعلق ب " لبث " وقيل: حال أي: مستقرا.

SAMIN-DURR:37:144/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:144/r2.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:37:144/r2.claim: Alternatively, في بطنه is circumstantial, meaning “settled there.”

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r1.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r1.claim: A marfūʿ report from Anas says Jonah heard the earth glorifying in the whale's depths and prayed; angels recognized his voice and interceded because of his accepted deeds and answered prayers in ease, so God ordered the whale to eject him. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r1.anchor: عن أنس مرفوعا من أنه عليه السلام لما التقمه الحوت وهوى به حتى انتهى إلى ما انتهى من الأرض سمع تسبيح الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r2.claim: Following Abū Ḥayyān, al-Ālūsī holds that Jonah would have remained alive in the whale until resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r2.anchor: واستظهر أبو حيان أن المراد بقوله سبحانه ( للبث في بطنه ( الخ لبقي في بطنه حيا إلى يوم البعث وبه أقول

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r3.claim: An objection says the living cannot remain until resurrection because reports say no human or animal with a soul survives the first trumpet blast.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r3.anchor: وتعقب بأنه ينافيه ما ورد من أنه لا يبقى عند النفخة الأولى ذو روح من البشر والحيوان

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī answers that, if such reports are accepted, the conditional wording can hyperbolically mean an exceedingly long period; alternatively, the resurrection day can include the trumpet as its precursor.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r4.anchor: بأنه مبالغة في طول المدة مع أنه في حيز لو فلا يرد رأسا أو الموت بوقت البعث ما يشمل زمان النفخة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r5.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r5.claim: Qatāda takes the verse to mean that the whale's belly would have become Jonah's grave until resurrection; the whale's body could endure without affliction until then.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r5.anchor: وعن قتادة لكان بطن الحوت قبرا له وظاهره أنه أريد للبث ميتا في بطنه إلى يوم البعث

ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r6.claim: The plural pronoun in “they are resurrected” has no explicit antecedent, which is apparent from the wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p144#3/r6.anchor: وضمير ( يبعثون ) لغير مذكور وهو ظاهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r9.claim: Without his glorification, the fish's belly would have been his grave until Resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r9.anchor: للبث في بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون} لصار بطن الحوت له قبرا إلى يوم القيامة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:144-146/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:144-146/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:144-146/r1.claim: The fish would have kept Jonah inside until the Resurrection, alive or dead.
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:144-146/r1.anchor: للبث فى بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون } حيا وقيل ميتا

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:144-146/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:144-146/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:144-146/r2.claim: The episode urges abundant remembrance of God and magnifies its importance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:144-146/r2.anchor: وفيه حث على إكثار الذكر وتعظيم لشأنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:144-146/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:144-146/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:144-146/r3.claim: Whoever turns to God in prosperity is helped by Him in adversity.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r4.claim: Without his prior glorification Jonah would have remained alive in the fish, or else become its food and have his parts mixed with it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r4.anchor: أي حيا أو بأن يكون غذاء له فتختلط أجزاؤه بأجزائه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r5.claim: The plural ending conveys resurrection of all creatures: a singular could exclude animals, while a dual could imply that only Jonah and the fish rise.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r6.claim: The passage alludes to the saying about knowing God in ease so He will know one in hardship, and urges remembrance while magnifying its importance.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r7.claim: Because Jonah remembered God in ease, God remembered and rescued him in hardship; the rescue was an astonishing act of divine greatness.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p342/r7.anchor: ولكنه لما كان ذكارا لله في حال الرخاء ذكرناه في حال الشدة

DURR-FULL:v7p120/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r5.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r5.claim: Tawus says the whale expelled Jonah sick; a gourd grew over him, later withered, and God rebuked him for grieving a plant but not a hundred thousand people.
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r5.anchor: قال طاوس: بلغني أنه لما نبذه الحوت بالعراء وهو سقيم نبتت عليه شجرة من يقطين

DURR-FULL:v7p125/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r1.claim: Al-Rabiʿ b. Anas explains Jonah’s prior righteous work as the reason for deliverance; the accompanying wisdom says good deeds raise their doer.
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r1.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس رضي الله عنه في قوله {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} قال: لولا أنه حلاله عمل صالح

DURR-FULL:v7p125/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r7.speaker: سعيد بن أبي الحسن
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r7.claim: Saʿid b. Abi al-Hasan says a history of worship and glorification rescued Jonah in distress; he remained in the whale forty days and nights before release and repentance.
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن أبي الحسن رضي الله عنه {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} قال: لولا أنه كان له سلف

DURR-FULL:v7p125/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r9.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak contrasts Jonah, who remembered God in ease and was rescued, with Pharaoh, who remembered only at drowning; Pharaoh’s late profession was rejected.
DURR-FULL:v7p125/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه قال: اذكروا الله في الرخاء يذكركم في الشدة فإن يونس عليه السلام

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas gives Jonah’s time in the whale as forty days.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: مكث يونس عليه السلام في بطن الحوت أربعين يوما

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj likewise says Jonah remained in the whale for forty days.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: بقي يونس في بطن الحوت أربعين يوما

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r5.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r5.claim: Abu Malik also reports that Jonah stayed in the whale forty days.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r5.anchor: عن أبي مالك رضي الله عنه قال: لبث يونس عليه السلام في بطن الحوت أربعين يوما

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r6.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr says Jonah remained inside for seven days, was carried through all the seas, then cast onto the bank of the Tigris.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال: لبث يونس في بطن الحوت سبعة أيام فطاف به البحار كلها

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r8.claim: Qatada says Jonah prayed often in ease and was saved; otherwise the whale’s belly would have become his grave until Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r8.anchor: وفي قوله {فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين} قال: كان كثير الصلاة في الرخاء فنجا

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r9.claim: Qatada identifies the endpoint “until they are raised” as the Day of Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r9.anchor: {إلى يوم يبعثون} قال: إلى يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v7p127/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r1.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r1.claim: Ikrima reports Jonah’s prayer from inside the whale: he lists his confinement and asks what good deed he has to offer; angels recognize his familiar voice in a strange place, and God identifies him as Jonah.
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: لما ذهب مغاضبا فكان في بطن الحوت قال من بطن الحوت

DURR-FULL:v7p127/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r2.claim: Ikrima says Jonah spent forty days in the whale, was cast out sick, and received a gourd plant whose shade, fruit, and root sustained him.
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r2.anchor: وكان في بطن الحوت أربعين يوما فنبذه الله {بالعراء وهو سقيم} وأنبت {عليه شجرة من يقطين}

DURR-FULL:v7p127/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r6.speaker: حميد بن هلال
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r6.claim: Hamid says Jonah’s body wasted away in the whale; after he invoked God and was cast ashore, the gourd fed him until his body recovered, then it dried and he wept.
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r6.anchor: فكان يونس في بطن الحوت حتى رق العظم وذهب اللحم والبشر والشعر وكان سقيما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r9.claim: The phrase means indefinitely: God may have caused the fish to die after swallowing Jonah, leaving both at the sea bottom until resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r9.anchor: بأن يميت الله الحوت حين ابتلاعه ويبقيهما في قعر البحر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r10.claim: Alternatively, a fish could have been trapped in something underwater and never surfaced, so Jonah would remain on the seabed until resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r10.anchor: أو بأن يختطف الحوت في حجر في البحر أو نحوه فلا يطفو على الماء حتى يبعث يونس يوم القيامة من قعر البحر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r3.claim: One group says Yūnus was rescued after an hour of daylight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r3.anchor: فقالت فرقة بعد ساعة من النهار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r4.claim: Another group says he was rescued after seven hours.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r5.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r5.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān says Yūnus remained in the whale three days.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان بعد ثلاثة أيام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r6.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ says he was rescued after seven days.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح بعد سبعة أيام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r7.claim: Another group says the period was fourteen days.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة بعد أربعة عشر يوما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r8.speaker: أبو مالك والسدي وابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r8.claim: Abū Mālik and al-Suddī say forty days; Ibn Jurayj says this is what reached him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r8.anchor: وقال أبو مالك والسدي بعد أربعين يوما، وهو قول ابن جريج أنه بلغه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r9.claim: Alongside God's prior decree, Yūnus's glorification is given as the reason for his rescue.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r9.anchor: وجعل تعالى علة استنقاذه مع القدر السابق تسبيحه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r1.claim: Qatāda says the whale’s belly would have been Jonah’s grave until resurrection, but God saved him because he prayed often in ease.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r1.anchor: قال قتادة لصار بطن الحوت له قبرا إلى يوم القيامة ولكنه كان كثير الصلاة في الرخاء فنجاه الله تعالى بذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك وكعب وأبو مالك وابن جريج والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r2.claim: One report says Jonah remained in the whale for forty days.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r2.anchor: أحدها أربعون يوما قاله أنس بن مالك وكعب وأبو مالك وابن جريج والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿAṭāʾ say Jonah remained in the whale for seven days.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r3.anchor: والثاني سبعة أيام قاله سعيد بن جبير وعطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r4.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda say Jonah remained in the whale for three days.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r4.anchor: والثالث ثلاثة أيام قاله مجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Jonah remained in the whale for twenty days.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r6.speaker: الشعبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r6.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the whale swallowed Jonah at forenoon and cast him out before sunset, so he stayed less than a day.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87#3/r6.anchor: والخامس بعض يوم التقمة ضحى ونبذه قبل غروب الشمس قاله الشعبي

BURSEVI:v7p380/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p380/r1.claim: God told the fish Jonah was not its food but a trust in its belly, forbade breaking bone or severing a joint, and kept him there forty nights, as inferred from his being cast ashore sick.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r1.anchor: روي أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى السمكة أني لم أجعله لك رزقا ولكن جعلت بطنك له وعاء فلا تكسري منه عظما

BURSEVI:v7p380/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v7p380/r2.claim: Kashifi says three or seven days is also reported, while forty is better known; the fish crossed seven seas and Jonah's flesh and skin became transparent so he could see its wonders while remembering God.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r2.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (سه روز ياهفت روز اشهر آنست كه هل روز درشكم ماهى بود وآن ماهى هفت دريارا بكشت

BURSEVI:v7p380/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p380/r5.claim: The verb allows either remaining alive or remaining dead in the fish's belly, until people are raised from their graves.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r5.anchor: {للبث} لمكث حيا أو ميتا {فى بطنه} أي : في بطن الحوت

BURSEVI:v7p380/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p380/r6.claim: The endpoint means the day creatures are raised from their graves.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r6.anchor: تاآن روز كه خلق را برانكيزند از قبور

BURSEVI:v7p380/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p380/r7.claim: Kashf al-Asrar gives three possibilities: Jonah and the fish both survive until resurrection; the fish dies but Jonah remains; or both die and its belly is Jonah's grave until resurrection.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r7.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : يبقى هو والحوت إلى يوم البعث.

BURSEVI:v7p380/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p380/r8.claim: Jonah's rescue because he glorified God urges abundant remembrance and magnifies its importance.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r8.anchor: فلم يلبث لكونه من المسبحين ، وفيه حث على إكثار الذكر وتعظيم لشأنه

BURSEVI:v7p380/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p380/r9.claim: When the heart is swallowed by the whale of the lower self, rescue comes through constant remembrance; turning to God in ease brings help in hardship, and good works support one who falls.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r9.anchor: وإشارة إلى أن خلاص يونس القلب إذا التقمه حوت النفس لا يكون إلا بملازمة ذكر الله

BURSEVI:v7p380/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p380/r10.speaker: الوسيط
BURSEVI:v7p380/r10.claim: Al-Wasit contrasts the remembering, righteous Jonah with forgetful, tyrannical Pharaoh, whose belief at drowning was rejected as too late.
BURSEVI:v7p380/r10.anchor: وفي الوسيط كان يونس عبدا صالحا ذاكرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.claim: Jonah's story was already recounted in Sura al-Anbiya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.anchor: قد تقدمت قصة يونس، عليه السلام، في سورة الأنبياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r1.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers the view that Jonah's prior worship in times of ease saved him; Ibn Kathir says a later report supports it if sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r1.anchor: قاله الضحاك بن قيس، وأبو العالية، ووهب بن منبه، وقتادة، وغير واحد. واختاره ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r7.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r7.claim: Anas, tentatively raising the report to the Prophet, says angels recognized Jonah's familiar prayer from a distant land; God recalled his accepted deeds and answered prayers in ease, then ordered the whale to cast him ashore.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p39/r7.anchor: أنه سمع أنس بن مالك -ولا أعلم إلا أن أنسا يرفع الحديث إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم-

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r14.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r14.claim: Qatada says the whale would have been Jonah's grave until Resurrection.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r14.anchor: قال قتادة : إلى يوم القيامة حتى يصير الحوت له قبرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r15.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r15.claim: Al-Sha'bi says the whale swallowed Jonah in the morning and released him that evening, after part of a day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r15.anchor: أحدها : بعض يوم , قال الشعبي : التقمه ضحى ولفظه عشية

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r18.speaker: أبو مالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r18.anchor: الرابع : أربعون يوما , قاله أبو مالك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r19.speaker: قيل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r19.claim: One report says the whale took Jonah past Eilat and returned by the Tigris to Nineveh.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r19.anchor: وقيل إنه سار بيونس حتى مر به إلى الإيلة ثم عاد في دجلة إلى نينوى

MUQATIL:37:141-144/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r7.claim: Without that devotion Jonah would have remained in the whale as punishment until people are raised from their graves.
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r7.anchor: عقوبة فيه { إلى يوم يبعثون } [آية: 144] الناس من قبورهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r1.claim: The apparent sense is that Jonah would have remained alive in the fish's belly until the Day of Resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r1.anchor: الظاهر لبثه حيا إلى يوم البعث

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r2.speaker: قتادة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r2.claim: Qatāda says the fish's belly would have been his grave until the Resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r2.anchor: وعن قتادة لكان بطن الحوت له قبرا إلى يوم القيامة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r3.claim: An unspecified report gives Jonah's stay in the fish as three days, seven days, or forty days.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r3.anchor: ود لبث فى بطنه ثلاثة أيام أو سبعة أو أربعين يوما

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r4.speaker: الشعبي
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the fish swallowed Jonah at midmorning and cast him out that evening.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#8/r4.anchor: وعن الشعبى التقمه ضحوة ولفظه عشية

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r14.claim: Without his prior praise and prayer, the whale’s belly would have been his grave until the Resurrection as punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r14.anchor: أي عقوبة له أي يكون بطن الحوت قبرا له إلى يوم القيامة

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r15.speaker: السدي والكلبي ومقاتل بن سليمان
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r15.claim: Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil ibn Sulayman say Yunus remained inside the whale for forty days.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r15.anchor: فقال السدي والكلبي ومقاتل بن سليمان: أربعين يوما

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r16.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r16.claim: Al-Dahhak says Yunus remained in the whale for twenty days.

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r17.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r17.claim: Ata says Yunus remained in the whale for seven days.

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r18.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r18.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says Yunus remained in the whale for three days.

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r19.claim: Another reported duration is a single hour; the author leaves the matter to God.

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet through Abu Hurayra says God ordered the whale to take Yunus without injuring flesh or breaking bone; Yunus heard sea creatures’ glorification, prayed, and was rescued after angels interceded, then was cast ashore sick.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.anchor: لما أراد الله تعالى ذكره حبس يونس في بطن الحوت أوحى الله إلى الحوت أن خذه

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r6.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r6.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says Yunus’s earlier good deeds prevented his remaining in the whale until Resurrection; wisdom teaches that good deeds raise a person after a stumble.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r6.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: لولا أنه كان له قبل ذلك عمل صالح

RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r1.claim: The excerpt opens mid-report: Allah helped the speaker against someone until that person accepted Islam; Razi says many hadiths concern this report.
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r1.anchor: ولا أنا إلا أن الله تعالى أعانني عليه فأسلم والأحاديث في ذلك كثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r2.claim: Razi argues that jinn were created from fire, citing Qur'an 15:27 and Satan's claim that he was created from fire while Adam was created from clay.
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r2.anchor: والدليل عليه قوله تعالى : ﴿ والجان خلقناه من قبل من نار السموم ﴾

RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r3.claim: Life in fire is plausible because physicians locate the soul's first attachment in the very hot heart; Galen says a dissected monkey's heart was extremely hot, and physicians attribute life to innate heat.
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r3.anchor: وقال جالينوس : إني بقرت مرة بطن قرد فأدخلت يدي في بطنه

RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r4.claim: Some hold it likely that the sphere of fire is filled with spiritual beings.
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الأغلب على الظن أن كرة النار تكون مملوءة من الروحانيات

RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r5.claim: One etymology derives jinn from concealment, with parallels in janna (ground veiled by trees), al-janna (which covers a person), majnun (mind concealed), janin (hidden in the womb), and jinnah as a protective screen; this would include angels unless common usage restricts the general term.
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r5.anchor: أن لفظ الجن مأخوذ من الاستتار ومنه الجنة لاستتار أرضها بالأشجار

RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r6.claim: A second etymology says jinn were named because they were initially custodians of the Garden.
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r6.anchor: والقول الثاني : أنهم سموا بهذا الاسم لأنهم كانوا في أول أمرهم خزان الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r7.claim: Razi judges the concealment etymology stronger than the custodians-of-the-Garden explanation.

RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r8.claim: Razi enumerates four accountable classes: angels, humans, jinn, and devils.
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r8.anchor: اعلم أن طوائف المكلفين أربعة : الملائكة والإنس والجن والشياطين

RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r9.claim: One view treats devils as a separate genus from jinn, just as humans and horses are distinct genera.
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r9.anchor: واختلفوا في الجن والشياطين فقيل : الشياطين جنس والجن جنس آخر كما أن الإنسان جنس والفرس جنس آخر

RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r10.claim: A second view includes good and evil among the jinn and calls the evil jinn devils.
RAZI-FULL:v1p75/r10.anchor: وقيل : الجن منهم أخيار ومنهم أشرار والشياطين اسم لأشرار الجن

STUDYQURAN:37:143/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r1.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r1.claim: IK and Ṭ say Jonah’s prior life of devotion prevented him from remaining in the fish until the Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r1.anchor: Had it not been for the life of devotion lived before these events, Jonah would have remained in the belly of the fish (IK, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:37:143/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r2.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r2.claim: A Prophetic saying urges people to know God in ease, so God will aid them in difficulty.
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r2.anchor: a saying of the Prophet Muhammad, “Seek to know God in times of ease, and He will know you

STUDYQURAN:37:143/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r5.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r5.claim: Aj says that without his praise, Jonah would have remained alive in the fish until human beings were resurrected.
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r5.anchor: the belly of the fish alive until the day on which human beings are resurrected (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:37:143/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r6.speaker: Aj, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r6.claim: Aj and Ṭ offer another reading: the fish’s belly would have served as Jonah’s grave until the Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:37:143/r6.anchor: the belly of the fish would have been his grave until the Day of Resurrection (Aj, Ṭ)

TAB-FULL:v19p627/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r1.claim: Jonah had worshipped and remembered God before the trial; God remembered him in distress and rescued him, instead of leaving him imprisoned in the whale until resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v19p627/r1.anchor: ولكنه كان من الذاكرين الله قبل البلاء، فذكره الله في حال البلاء، فأنقذه ونجاه

TAB-FULL:v19p630/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r4.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r4.claim: In a sermon, al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays urges people to remember God in ease so He remembers them in hardship, citing Jonah's remembrance and Pharaoh's failed belief at drowning.
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r4.anchor: الضحاك بن قيس، يقول على منبره

TAB-FULL:v19p631/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p631/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p631/r1.claim: Qatāda says the whale's belly would have become Jonah's grave until the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v19p631/r1.anchor: قتادة، قوله: {للبث في بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون} [الصافات: 144] : «لصار له بطن الحوت قبرا إلى يوم القيامة»

TAB-FULL:v19p631/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p631/r2.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB-FULL:v19p631/r2.claim: Abū Mālik reports that Jonah remained in the whale's belly for forty days.
TAB-FULL:v19p631/r2.anchor: السدي، عن أبي مالك، قال: «لبث يونس في بطن الحوت أربعين يوما»

TABATABAI:37:143-148/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r5.claim: Remaining in the fish until resurrection means remaining there perpetually until raised and brought out, like a person remaining in the grave; the author links this to 20:55.
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r5.anchor: تأبيد مكثه في بطنه إلى أن يبعث فيخرج منه كالقبر الذي يقبر فيه الإنسان

TABATABAI:37:143-148/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r6.claim: The verse does not establish whether Jonah would remain alive or dead, whether the fish's body remained intact, which trumpet blast is meant, or whether resurrection idiomatically signals a long time.
TABATABAI:37:143-148/r6.anchor: ولا دلالة في الآية على كونه عليه السلام على تقدير اللبث حيا في بطن الحوت إلى يوم يبعثون

TABRISI:37:142-147/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:37:142-147/r17.claim: Without his being among those who praised God, Jonah’s belly in the whale would have become his grave until the resurrection.
TABRISI:37:142-147/r17.anchor: أي لصار بطن الحوت قبرا له إلى يوم القيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r1.claim: Mujahid says Jonah's frequent prayer and remembrance in ease spared him from remaining in the whale as punishment until resurrection; al-Kalbi agrees.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: فلولا أنه كان في الرخاء قبل أن يلتقمه الحوت، {من المسبحين} يعني المصلين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r4.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r4.claim: Al-Rabi b. Anas says that without Jonah's righteous deeds he would have remained in the whale.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r4.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: كان خلاله عمل صالح للبث في بطنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r5.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak b. Qays urges remembrance in ease so God remembers one in hardship, contrasting Jonah with Pharaoh, who remembered only while drowning and was rebuked.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r5.anchor: قال الضحاك بن قيس (¬3) (¬4): اذكروا الله في الرخاء يذكركم في الشدة، فإن يونس كان عبدا صالحا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r7.speaker: ابن جريج والسدي عن أبي مالك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj and al-Suddi, reporting from Abu Malik, say Jonah stayed in the whale forty days; al-Kalbi gives the same duration.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r7.anchor: وقال ابن جريج والسدي عن أبي مالك: لبث يونس في بطن الحوت أربعين يوما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r8.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r8.claim: Muqatil b. Hayyan says Jonah stayed in the whale three days.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r8.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: ثلاثة أيام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r9.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r9.claim: Ata says Jonah stayed in the whale seven days.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r10.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says Jonah stayed in the whale twenty days.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r13.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r13.claim: Al-Hasan says Jonah did not pray inside the whale but had already done good; he remained only a short time and was expelled well after being swallowed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r13.anchor: قال الحسن: ما كانت له صلاة في بطن الحوت ولكنه قدم عملا صالحا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r14.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r14.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that angels heard Jonah's faint glorification, recalled his past good deeds, interceded, and God ordered the whale to cast him onto shore.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p107/r14.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r6.claim: Without his prior worship, Jonah would have remained in the fish's belly until the Day of Resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r6.anchor: في بطن الحوت إلى يوم القيامة

ELMALILI:37:139-179/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r6.claim: Without that, Yunus would have remained in the fish’s belly until the day of resurrection.
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r6.anchor: her hâlde baʿs olunacakları güne kadar onun karnında kalırdı

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.claim: Alusi transmits the People of the Book's account: sent to Nineveh, overwhelmed by its wickedness, Yunus fled toward Tarshish via Jaffa and boarded a ship caught in a storm.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.anchor: Âlûsî tefsirinde der ki: “Yûnus aleyhisselâm hakkında ehl-i kitâbın kitaplarında mezkur olan şudur

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r17.claim: Had Yunus not been one of the frequent glorifiers, he would have remained in the fish until the day people are resurrected; he did not remain there.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r17.anchor: ba‘s olunacakları güne kadar elbette onun karnında kalırdı lâkin kalmadı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.claim: These verses briefly report what befell Jonah after he left his homeland; the Qur’an foregrounds the story’s instructive lesson rather than supplying bare history.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.anchor: Kur’an’ın amacı, salt tarihî bilgi vermek değil, olayın ibret verici yönünü öne çıkarmak olduğu için onun hayatı hakkında daha fazla ayrıntı vermeye gerek görülmemiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.speaker: Kitâb-ı Mukaddes
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.claim: The Bible’s fuller account broadly matches the Qur’an: sent to warn Nineveh, Jonah flees by ship toward Tarshish, is cast overboard by lot in a storm and swallowed; after prayer he is returned ashore, recommissioned, and Nineveh repents.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.anchor: Kitâb-ı Mukaddes’te Hz. Yûnus hakkında genel hatlarıyla Kur’an’da verilenlerle de uyuşan daha ayrıntılı bilgi bulunmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r13.claim: The counterfactual means that without being a good servant, Jonah would have died inside the fish and remained there until resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r13.anchor: yani o, iyi bir kul olmasaydı balık kendisini yutacak, orada ölecek ve tekrar dirilmesi kıyamete kalacaktı.

BURHAN:v4p379/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p379/r1.speaker: ابن الشجري
BURHAN:v4p379/r1.claim: Ibn al-Shajari objects that substitution is the strongest parsing for an exception after negation, though accusative is allowed; its use in both verses suggests a positive construction, answered by the author's point that negation is implicit.
BURHAN:v4p379/r1.anchor: وقال ابن الشجري هذا يخالف أصح الإعرابين لأن المستثنى بعد النفي يقوى فيه البدل

BURHAN:v4p379/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p379/r3.speaker: الخليل
BURHAN:v4p379/r3.claim: Ibn Barjan quotes al-Khalil that Qur'anic لولا means هلا except in Jonah's case, where its answer differs; the author questions this exception.
BURHAN:v4p379/r3.anchor: ونقل ابن برجان في تفسيره في أواخر سورة هود عن الخليل إن جميع ما في القرآن من لولا

NAHHAS:v3p438/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p438/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p438/r15.claim: A wisdom saying says righteous action raises its doer; Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports that after Jonah prayed, the whale cast him out.
NAHHAS:v3p438/r15.anchor: ومكتوب في الحكمة أن العمل الصالح يرفع ربه إذا عشر قال سعيد بن جبير لما قال لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r5.claim: Jonah’s being among those who glorified God prevented his remaining in the fish until resurrection; this is another original conditional use of lولا.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r5.anchor: وفي الصافات : ﴿ فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين للبث

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r1.claim: The descriptive form marks a settled trait: Yunus was rescued from distress through his sustained practice of glorification.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r1.anchor: والمجيء بالصيغة الوصفية هنا إشارة إلى أن مداومة التسبيح تخلِّص من الكروب والمكاره، وأن يونس إنما نجا من هذه الشدة بمداومة التسبيح
